title: You're Not Getting Promoted Because You're Too Good At Your Job
summary: Explores how individual execution excellence and being indispensable in a specialized role can paradoxically prevent career advancement to higher-level positions; discusses the tension between deep technical expertise and the broader leadership and leverage expected at senior levels.
when-to-read: Read this article when you're wondering why strong technical performance and problem-solving skills haven't translated to promotions or advancement, or when evaluating what skills matter most for the next level of your career. If you're instead looking for specific technical advice on how to improve your debugging or execution skills, consult articles tagged with code-quality or problem-solving instead.
